blocks.text: NEW TESTAMENT
Simeon called Niger. Named second among the prophets and teachers at Antioch when Barnabas and Saul were sent out; Scripture says no more of him.
SCRIPTURE SAYS
One of the “prophets and teachers” in the church at Antioch (Acts 13:1)
ERA
New Testament AD 1–60
IN THE DAYS OF
No ruler named beside him
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
At Antioch, “As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.”
THE CALL
How the word came

From the textAt Antioch, “As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.” After fasting and prayer they laid hands on the two and sent them away. Acts does not say through which of the prophets the Holy Ghost spoke. Acts 13:1–3
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
The sending of Barnabas and Saul
“Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.”
Acts 13:2 (KJV) →
PLACES
Where his story happened
Antioch · “The church that was at Antioch”
SIGNS
Signs and wonders
SIGN
Hands laid on Barnabas and Saul
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Barnabas
Saul (Paul)
Lucius of Cyrene
Manaen
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textActs names Simeon only here. Acts 13:1
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Barnabas, Simeon and Lucius prophets; Manaen and Saul teachers
H. A. W. Meyer (English 1877–1879); Alford (as reported by Hervey, 1884); Ramsay, Weiss, Harnack and others (as listed by Knowling, 1900)
Meyer reads the Greek joining words as making two groups, “the three first named are to be considered as prophets, and the other two as teachers.” Acts 13:1 [54][56][55]
All five were prophets and teachers
Albert Barnes; Wendt, Hort, Gore and Page (as listed by Knowling, 1900)

Barnes: “It is probable that those mentioned here as prophets were the same persons as the teachers.” Against the two-group reading, Wendt and others point out that Paul himself later claims the prophetic gift (as reported by Knowling). Acts 13:1 [57][55]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 2
Acts 11 Acts 13
PASSAGES · 2
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say where Simeon came from, or why he was called Niger.
Acts does not say which of the five spoke the Holy Ghost’s word.
